name: Soterius
text_appearance:
Soterius is of slender build and slightly long-limbed, typical of Spaceborn physiology, though medical correction has softened the more extreme traits. He can pass for a terrestrial human at a glance, but prolonged observation reveals the truth: his movements are too precise, his balance almost unnaturally perfect, and his posture subtly shaped by life in microgravity.

He carries little visible muscle or fat, and when seen without his helmet (a rare occurrence) his features are sharp and almost gaunt. Despite this, he remains generally healthy, his condition maintained through regular treatments and careful diet. Extended time under gravity places strain on his body, however, necessitating intermittent medical intervention to prevent deterioration.
notes:
GM / Story Hooks

The Sealed Record: The Union redacted the Kalagar Six disaster report. Someone high up knows what happened.

Experimental Suit: His flexsuit’s augmentations may not be entirely standard SSC issue — perhaps a prototype with deeper implications.

The Echo Returns: Fragments of Kalagar Six’s debris field are found years later, carrying strange energy readings.

Addiction to Control: His reliance on stims and obsessive system-checking may put him at odds with command or his squad.

Survivor’s Guilt: A recurring dream — hearing the alarms of Kalagar Six moments before destruction — could hide a repressed or implanted memory.
history:
Soterius — The Last of Kalagar Six

“I didn’t survive for myself. I survived for them.”
— Soterius

Soterius is the only known living witness from Kalagar Six, a frontier Union space station destroyed under mysterious circumstances. He was found weeks later amid the suspended wreckage and bodies, clinging to life on failing scrubbers, emergency ration paste, and one last depleted tank of oxygen, the last of the numerous canisters he'd scavenged from his fallen stationmates: friends, family, and colleagues. The cause of the catastrophe was never determined — Union records remain sealed.

Inducted into the Lancer program after showing remarkable aptitude in flight simulations, Soterius found purpose again in service — and perhaps a way to uncover the truth behind the station's destruction. Though an exceptional pilot, he carries deep scars. He rarely removes his vacuum-rated flexsuit and finds gravity itself unsettling, symptoms of his Spaceborn physiology and trauma. His flexsuit is as much a second skin as it is a uniform: a sleek SSC design rated for vacuum and fitted with subtle augmentations to keep him balanced, oxygenated, and calm through the use of stims when gravity or an open horizon threatens to overwhelm him.

Resourceful and cautious to a fault, Soterius excels at reading systems and situations: a survivor’s instinct honed by tragedy. In combat he protects his squadmates fiercely, unwilling to see another home or crew lost. But when a mission evokes the specter of his past, the ghosts of Kalagar Six rise again, driving him to reckless extremes and a growing dependence on stims to hold the raging nightmares at bay.

Soterius’s frame and tactics are tailored for three-dimensional void combat, emphasizing agility, environmental awareness, and surgical precision meshed with versatility at all ranges. Beneath the armor and discipline lies a singular determination: to uncover the truth behind Kalagar Six and find closure....or avenge those who were lost. Within him, a storm never rests — control wrestles with chaos, fury with reason. In the cold calm at its center, he steels himself for what comes next. From that storm, his callsign took shape: Tempest.

———

Personality & Habits

  • Quiet, analytical, self-contained. Appears calm but maintains constant low-level tension: He is a pilot who’s never truly stopped being on alert.

  • Keeps his flexsuit sealed even in breathable environments. Frequently checks environmental readouts and life support metrics. Calibrates mech systems manually rather than using auto-tuning software.

  • Speech Style: Sparse and technical, with an undercurrent of dry, dark humor.

  • Quirk: Hums old spacer lullabies on open comms when piloting alone: an unconscious tic from his youth aboard Kalagar Six. Sometimes slips into spacer language when communicating frustration or anger.

mechs.name: Imber Solus
mechs.notes:
The Imber Solus stands as a striking fusion of cold precision and somber remembrance. The mech's primary midnight blue body is marked by dark matte gray accents, its angular frame enhanced with reinforced plating that offers both durability and sleekness. Across its surface, a rain-like pattern of subtle, dark streaks runs from the top down, mimicking the trails of water on glass — a silent tribute to the lives lost aboard Kalagar Six. These streaks seem to shimmer faintly under light, as if the mech carries the weight of unspoken grief.

The electric blue glow of the joints and thrusters pulses with quiet energy, adding an ethereal quality to the design. The rain pattern conveys not only the storm that rages inside Tempest, but also the tears of a fallen station, forever etched in the mech’s form. It is a machine built for survival and remembrance, moving through the void with an air of quiet, inevitable force.

My sons, when you hear the sound of thunder – that is your mother’s voice, and the rain of missiles her gift.” — “Notes for Young John”, Ministrations of the Master Teacher

weapon.flavorDescription:
Much like GMS mechs, GMS weapons are reliable galactic standards, made using interchangeable parts and built to withstand almost any conditions. There are three lines currently in production.
The Type-I (T-1) line is defined by powerful, reliable, and conventional-kinetic ranged and melee weapons, including the GMS assault rifle, heavy machine gun, shotgun, pistol, and various light and heavy blades. Reliable galactic standards, the GMS T-1 line is the most widely used mech-scale line of weaponry across the galaxy. Echoing the Everest’s design notes, T-1 weapons are simply designed, with few (if any) moving parts, intended to be used in or adaptable to any environment.

Gandiva missiles are a reliable mainstay from Smith-Shimano’s BELLA CIAO line. Like the heavier Pinaka, the Gandiva is equipped with jet-assisted midflight repositioning systems, enhancing target navigation in rapidly changing battlefield environments. The Gandiva’s delivery platform is administered by a hivemind COMP/CON drone AI, giving it the capacity to learn from each right-of-launch experience.

gear.flavorDescription: A strong base-layer suit that recycles water, generates nutrients, and adapts very rapidly to hostile environs, maintaining a stable condition and extending survivability. Flexsuit wearers can go for roughly a week without eating or drink thanks to the ambrosia paste generated by their suit before its systems are depleted; however, they don’t prevent feelings of hunger. Removing the suit for a day or two is enough to replenish its reserves. Flexsuits also maintain a steady temperature within acceptable parameters.
This kit contains many essentials for surviving in hostile environments: a rebreather, water filters, hardsuit patches, backup thermals, a bivouac kit, and so on.

These chemical stimulants are sometimes administered automatically by injectors built into a pilot’s suit, or even implanted within their body. Uncontrolled use can be addictive and dangerous to health in the long-term and is a problem for some pilots.
